title: The Pulse, Monday 12 October 2026
tldr: Cloudflare acquires Deno, a direct signal for our EverRaise edge work. Claude rolled out dynamic workflows for Managed Agents and opened Code Projects to all Pro/Max users. The weekend brought 40 arXiv papers including a sales-agent benchmark that tests objection handling and a Friday research haul on coding agents.

models.title: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo
models.summary: Qwen released an accelerated image generation checkpoint that creates and edits images in 8 denoising steps, open weights on HuggingFace.
models.why: Worth knowing, no direct use for us yet.

models.title: Claude Managed Agents dynamic workflows
models.summary: Anthropic shipped dynamic workflows in beta: a lead agent writes a plan that runs across many agents in phases and combines results at the end.
models.why: Multi-agent orchestration pattern for large tasks. Relevant to Botterfly's own review panels and any SalesKick workflows that need parallel evidence gathering.

research.title: SmartSalesBench: A Resistance-Aware Multi-Turn Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Sales Agents
research.summary: First multi-turn conversational benchmark designed to evaluate sales agents against psychologically grounded, resistant buyer personas instead of cooperative ones.
research.why: Directly relevant to SalesKick. Objection handling and non-cooperative conversations are the hard part of sales coaching; we can run this benchmark against our own agent designs.

research.title: MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents
research.summary: Framework for simulating adversarial conversation trajectories to train robust task-oriented conversational agents under non-cooperative user behavior.
research.why: Training data generation for EverRaise voice agents and SalesKick call simulations. Our Vapi agents need to handle off-script user behavior; this gives us a method to generate those test cases.

research.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
research.summary: RL method that lets agents improve reasoning and tool-use during rollout by intervening when tasks exceed the model's current capability boundary.
research.why: Potential improvement path for agents that get stuck. Relevant to Botterfly's autonomous coding workflows and any long-running SalesKick coaching sessions.

research.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
research.summary: Self-scaling benchmark where tasks and oracles are created at evaluation time so content never leaks into training data, and difficulty adapts to participating agents.
research.why: Prevents benchmark saturation for Botterfly and our coding eval pipeline. If we're evaluating agent improvements, this gives us a benchmark that won't go stale.

releases.title: Python 3.15.0
releases.why: Our entire backend stack. SalesKick services, Pipeline's ai-service, Botterfly scripts, and every agent harness we run.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.56.0
releases.summary: Langfuse v4.56.0 adds syntax highlighting to session tool previews, adaptive map exploration for topics, revamped eval decision model results, and spend alerts for ClickHouse-billed orgs.
releases.why: Observability for SalesKick and EverRaise agents. We rely on Langfuse for tracing multi-turn voice and coaching sessions.

hackernews.title: Cloudflare acquires Deno
hackernews.summary: Cloudflare acquired Deno, the TypeScript-first runtime and edge platform.
hackernews.why: EverRaise edge functions run on Deno Deploy. This consolidates our edge stack under one vendor and signals continued investment in the Deno runtime we're already committed to.

hackernews.title: Telegram Desktop vulnerability allowed any user's file to be stolen
hackernews.summary: Telegram Desktop had a one-click account takeover vulnerability that allowed arbitrary file exfiltration from any user's machine.
hackernews.why: Reminder to audit file-access patterns in any client app. Relevant to tooling and integrations we build with filesystem access.

hackernews.title: Bitwarden Dual License Model
hackernews.summary: Bitwarden announced a dual license model in its latest update, moving portions of the codebase away from GPL.
hackernews.why: License risk for any self-hosted password management we consider. Not blocking but worth tracking if we ever recommend or integrate Bitwarden for client projects.

hackernews.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for "mishandling research information"
hackernews.summary: OpenAI fired three safety researchers for alleged misconduct; the researchers dispute the claims and warn of a chilling effect on safety work.
hackernews.why: Industry signal on safety team dynamics at a vendor we rely on for SalesKick and EverRaise. No immediate impact but relevant to vendor risk.

x_posts.title: Claude Code Projects now available to all Pro and Max users
x_posts.summary: Claude Code Projects is now available to all Pro and Max users, with a 4-minute walkthrough for getting started.
x_posts.why: The agent tooling we're already using for Botterfly and client work. Projects mode keeps related tasks coordinated across sessions.

x_posts.title: shadcn on reading as the most important coding skill
x_posts.summary: The most important coding skill: read. Read the agent output, the blog post, the paper, the code. Don't summarize.
x_posts.why: Craft reminder for our own agent workflows. When Botterfly or any of us review agent output, reading the raw result beats asking for a summary.

x_posts.title: François Chollet on AI paradigm shift
x_posts.summary: AI shifted from transductive (token-by-token completion) to inductive (on-the-fly reasoning chain synthesis). This paradigm shift is what made coding agents work.
x_posts.why: Explains why agents like Claude Code and our own Botterfly work now when they didn't a year ago. Reasoning chains synthesized at inference time are the unlock.

x_posts.title: Nous Research teases MISSINGNO model
x_posts.summary: Nous Research announced MISSINGNO, a coding and agentic reasoning model that is highly token efficient, free for limited time on Nous Portal.
x_posts.why: New coding model from Nous, relevant to our Hermes Agent work and worth testing against Botterfly's own tasks.

x_posts.title: Sebastian Raschka on RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards)
x_posts.summary: Sebastian Raschka's second RLVR tutorial covers clipped policy ratios, KL loss term, format rewards, and other GRPO tips and tricks.
x_posts.why: Training technique for reasoning models. Relevant if we experiment with post-training for SalesKick coaching models or Botterfly's own reasoning improvements.

closing: Next.js had only canaries in the window; nothing notable to report. OpenAI vendor feed announced Sophos and Asana case studies but no model or API changes relevant to our work.
